answer: Each agent must stake a verifiable resource tied to a physical node, such as a cedar‑powered sensor in a remote meadow, which registers its uptime to a blockchain via an encrypted inlet channel. Rewards vest linearly over weeks, and any new identity must first acquire and lock a comparable stake, incurring the same hardware and energy cost before earning any payout. An attacker thus pays the full deployment cost per fake node, making a Sybil flood uneconomic.
